title: Reusable modules, the registry, and versioning what you publish

videos.script: Ana's shop has a network: a VPC and two subnets. Now the analytics team wants one just like it. {{copy}} She could copy the files. Then there would be two networks, and two places to fix every mistake. {{module}} A module is the other way. Any directory of Terraform files can be called from another one. Values go in, and outputs come out. {{call}} You will write a network module, call it twice, and read the address it gives each resource. {{addresses}} Then the module moves to a Git repository, at a tagged version. Every configuration that uses it chooses when to upgrade. {{git}} The hard part is changing it afterwards. A rename that looks harmless plans to destroy three subnets for whoever calls it. One block inside the module turns that into nothing at all. {{moved}} You will also see what makes a version major, where the public registry fits, and why a stranger's module runs with your credentials. {{registry}}
